items.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs — Ilia Shumailov & Alexander Panfilov
items.summary:
Tim Scarfe speaks with Ilia Shumailov and Alexander Panfilov about their paper, Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs.

The core bug sounds deceptively simple: providers return encrypted reasoning state so conversations can be resumed or forked. But those blobs can be replayed across users and sibling models. A smaller model can ask the provider to decrypt the trace, then repeat the hidden reasoning in plain text. The discussion covers leaked private data, a broadly reusable jailbreak, poisoned agent traces, chain-of-thought monitoring, responsible disclosure, and possible defenses.

Ilia Shumailov is an AI and security researcher, formerly at Google DeepMind, who completed his Cambridge PhD under Ross Anderson. Alexander Panfilov is a PhD researcher at the ELLIS Institute Tübingen and the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, working on AI safety, adversarial machine learning, and LLM red-teaming. They close by separating the demonstrated jailbreaking threat from ordinary benign distillation, and by arguing for controlled experiments over sweeping claims.

TIMESTAMPS:

00:01:33 Portable encrypted thought and decoded reasoning
00:24:55 How the attack works and what it means
00:39:04 Doom, defense, and scientific restraint

items.title: Harnessed Agentic RL w/ LEGO-RL & Co-RL Solutions
items.summary:
We are witnessing a mathematical and coding crisis at the very frontier of Harnessed Agentic AI. 

While breakthrough frameworks like LEGO-RL (see also my video from yesterday) have finally stopped models from "cheating" their way through chaotic coding environments, they’ve forced us to confront a terrifying new bottleneck: how do we train new AI models (also the ever more prominent MoE models) on advanced RL, since our classical RL math breaks down? 

Academia and industry's boldest answer is Co-RL: a system that completely removes human labels by pitting different model architectures against each other in an unsupervised, multi-agent peer-review panel. It promises infinite, self-correcting intelligence. 

But when we look closely at the underlying mathematics, a fatal structural flaw emerges. If you believe that throwing Qwen, Llama, and Gemma into a room together is a guaranteed path to awaited  "superintelligence", you urgently need to understand the mathematical illusion of the "shared blind spot", before it collapses your entire RL training run.

items.title: The Wildest Smartphone I’ve Ever Seen 🤯
items.summary:
This is the wildest smartphone camera I’ve seen yet. 🤯

HONOR's new Robot Phone has a 200MP camera mounted on a motorized titanium gimbal that literally unfolds out of the phone and can move up to 360° per second.

They even partnered with ARRI—the company behind some of Hollywood’s most popular cinema cameras—to build it.

The rest of the phone is equally ridiculous, with Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 powering the whole thing.

It starts at around $1,400 and, for now, is only available in China.

Would you actually buy a phone with a camera like this?

items.title: India Doesn't Have Enough GPUs: Here's Why | Jarvislabs.ai Founder On AI Infrastructure
items.summary:
India’s AI ambitions are growing fast, but is the country ready with the infrastructure to support them?

In this episode, we sit down with Vishnu Subramanian, Founder of Jarvislabs.ai, to unpack the infrastructure challenges shaping India’s AI future- from the rising cost and availability of GPUs to data centres, compute economics, open-source AI and India’s dependence on global hyperscalers.

Vishnu shares how the AI infrastructure landscape has changed since he started Jarvislabs.ai, why simply adding more data centres may not be enough, and what India needs to do differently to build a globally competitive AI ecosystem.

The podcast also discusses:
- Why GPU costs have skyrocketed
- Is India running out of AI compute?
- Why AI infrastructure is becoming a financial problem
- Does India need its own AI cloud?
- Building smarter and more efficient data centres
- Open-source vs closed-source AI
- What India should do with ₹10,000 crore for AI
- Why Indian IT companies need to think bigger
- The future of AI infrastructure and sovereign AI
- How students and young engineers can prepare for the AI era
- Why India needs a stronger AI research ecosystem

Watch the full conversation to understand what it will really take for India to build and scale its AI infrastructure.

CHAPTERS:
0:00 Introduction & the evolution of JarvisLabs.ai
2:00 The soaring cost of GPUs, RAM, and hardware infrastructure
5:10 Transitioning from individual Kagglers to global startups & enterprises
7:15 Ambition gap: Why Indian founders need to target global scale
10:05 Re-engineering data center efficiency instead of copying Western rules
14:50 Hardware CapEx vs. Large Language Model training complexity
17:35 The case for open source: Avoiding proprietary lock-in
21:50 Should India build closed-source frontier models?
25:50 The future of Indian IT services in the age of forward deployed engineers
28:40 Hardware choices: RTX Pro 6000 vs. H100/H200 NVLink clusters
33:40 Why "vibe coding" fails for complex, high-reliability enterprise systems
38:55 Using AI for deep curiosity vs. completing homework
42:00 Building an Indian ecosystem that fosters high-risk AI research

items.title: Most People Just Get AI Slop
items.summary: In episode 1019 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, @JonKrohnLearns talks with Priyanka Vergadia, better known to her quarter million strong developer community as the cloud girl, about building effective 'skills' in Claude AI. She details her process of breaking down complex tasks, like writing a blog, into explicit sub-tasks with specific prompts, and even incorporating human-in-the-loop steps for review and refinement. This method ensures a much more personalized and higher-quality AI output, moving beyond generic responses to truly leverage the tool's capabilities.
